text:
Alex Chen: Heads-up - Mosaic's pre-sales asked for a concrete interop smoke plan before Wed. They want route parity, retry semantics, and any SDK differences documented. Can we lock owners?
Maria Gomez: I'll lead acceptance tests for semantic parity and edge-case prompts. Will need a representative prompt set from Mosaic (10 categories).
Tyler Patel: I'll own the proxy and behavior mapping. Important: Mosaic's API uses idempotency keys and expects 202 + status polling for long-running. Redwood returns streaming + 200. We should emulate both flows.
Sophie Li: Security side: they asked about cross-region data residency and webhook callbacks to customer endpoints. Need to confirm our webhook signing, rotation, and optional IP allowlisting.
Ethan Brooks: Pricing note: Mosaic procurement wants a POC invoice line with capped token spend and overage grace. Propose $8k credit + 7 day grace period. Thoughts?
Alex Chen: OK. @Ethan hold on the exact number until Sales Ops confirms. For now signal capped credit. Maria, add tolerance thresholds for diffs.
Maria Gomez: Draft acceptance thresholds: - semantic match (BLEU-like similarity) >= 0.87 on canonical set - top-1 token match >= 80% after normalization - streaming chunk order preserved 99% - no PII leakage in outputs.
Tyler Patel: Implementation notes: create a compatibility proxy container that does: 1) map model names (mosaic->rwd) 2) support both streaming and poll patterns 3) rewrite idempotency headers 4) normalize timestamps/uuids. Quick example curl for poll flow:
```bash
# poll-style request
curl -X POST https://compat.redwood.test/v1/async -d '{"model":"mosaic-32","prompt":"hi"}' -H 'Idempotency-Key: abc123'
# returns 202 with status_url
curl https://compat.redwood.test/status/xyz -> {"status":"succeeded","result_url":"..."}
```
Maria Gomez: I'll run 1k prompts from their categories initially. Any objections to synthetic variants (typos, whitespace) to see normalization effects?
Sophie Li: No objections. Also record retention: on-hosted we keep logs 30 days by default, can offer longer via enterprise add-on. Webhook signing: we use HMAC-SHA256 with rotating keys (doc: https://redwood-internal/security/webhooks).
infra-bot: KMS integration check: Private deployment supports customer KMS (AWS KMS & Azure Key Vault). Hosted BYOK via KMS bridge requires legal onboarding.
Ethan Brooks: I'll draft the POC terms and include a clause for Dedicated eval pricing if they want guaranteed tail latency.
Alex Chen: Action items: Tyler: deploy proxy image to staging and add runbook; Maria: define canonical prompt list and run harness; Sophie: finalize security answers and webhook doc link; Ethan: draft credit + MSA addendum.
Tyler Patel: ETA for proxy smoke: tomorrow 11am PT. I'll push image to registry.redwood/ci/mosaic-compat:v0.2 and post curl examples.
Maria Gomez: After smoke I will run the 1k canonical set and post a short report with diffs and similarity scores. If similarity < threshold we'll escalate to ML for prompt templates.
Sophie Li: Uploaded security answers draft to https://redwood-internal/poqs/mosaic-2026 - marked 4 questions for infra clarifications.
infra-bot: TODOs created: "Confirm webhook ip ranges" assigned to Eng Infra; "Confirm BYOK legal steps" assigned to Security.
Alex Chen: Good. One more: Mosaic asked about model drift detection — include a short line about our quality monitoring and eval alerts (Redwood Optimize).
Maria Gomez: Noted. I'll attach an example alert rule (if semantic score drops >10% over a week).
Ethan Brooks: I'll follow up with Sales Ops on the credit figure and pre-approve the procurement email template.
Tyler Patel: Quick dev note: mapping table will include fallback to a smaller model if quota exceeded. Will document expected behavior in proxy README.
Alex Chen: Thanks team. Keep this thread updated with links to the smoke logs. If legal signs the addendum we'll kick off Wed morning.
note: sales presales thread coordinating a compatibility smoke plan for migrating from a competitor's API; includes owners, proxy sketch, acceptance thresholds, security notes, and POC credit discussion
